gloss: be full, fill; fulfil, complete; fullness
summary: The verb is to be full or to fill: a skin with water, sacks with grain, the earth with men, a house with the cloud of Yahweh's glory. From that it is to complete a set time (“her days were full to give birth”, “when seventy years are full”) and to fulfil a word (“to fulfil the word of Yahweh”, “he spoke with his mouth and fulfilled with his hand”). Three fixed uses come from it: “fill the hand” of a man to install him as priest, from the portions put into the priests' palms at their installation (the מִלֻּאִים); “fill after Yahweh”, to follow him wholly, said of Caleb and Joshua; and filling a gold setting with stones. The adjective מָלֵא is “full”, and the nouns מְלֹא “fullness, what fills” (“the earth and its fullness”) and מְלֵאָה “the full yield” of field and winepress. The Aramaic of Daniel, the Peshitta's word for the New Testament's “fulfil” and “fullness”, Akkadian malû, Ugaritic, Phoenician and Sabaean mlʾ and Arabic malaʾa share the sense.

words.gloss: be full, fill; be fulfilled, complete; fulfil; fill the hand (install as priest); follow wholly; set (stones)
words.summary: About 250 times in the Old Testament, in the qal, niphal and piel, with one pual and one hithpael. The count from its key (285) takes in some 33 tokens of the adjective מָלֵא, which is spelt alike. What fills is usually put without a preposition (וַתִּמָּלֵא הָאָרֶץ חָמָס, “the earth was filled with violence”, Gen 6:11, has no word for “with”), and the same verb serves for filling a place, completing a time, and fulfilling a word.

stems.gloss: be full; fill; be fulfilled (of days); the heart is full (to do)

senses.definition: To be full, or full of something: a river to its banks, a winepress, the earth of violence, of Yahweh's covenant faithfulness or of the knowledge of Yahweh, a man of power or of words.

evidence.note: “The end of all flesh has come before me, כִּי־מָלְאָה הָאָרֶץ חָמָס”: the earth is full of violence.
“The Jordan מָלֵא over all its banks all the days of harvest”: full to overflowing.
“Come, tread, for the winepress is full (מָלְאָה), the vats overflow.”
“The covenant faithfulness of Yahweh fills the earth (מָלְאָה הָאָרֶץ)”; also Psa 119:64.
“The earth is full of your creatures.”
“They shall not hurt or destroy in all my holy mountain, כִּי־מָלְאָה הָאָרֶץ דֵּעָה אֶת־יַהְוֶה as the waters cover the sea.”
“I am full (מָלֵאתִי) of power, the spirit of Yahweh, and justice and might, to declare to Jacob his transgression.”
Elihu: “I am full of words; the spirit in my belly constrains me.”
“I am full of the heat of Yahweh; I am weary of holding it in.”
“The land is full of judgment of blood, and the city is full of violence.”

senses.definition: To fill a place so that it holds no more: men the earth, the cloud of Yahweh's glory the tabernacle and the house, Yahweh himself heaven and earth.

evidence.note: “Be fruitful and multiply וּמִלְאוּ אֶת־הָאָרֶץ and subdue it.”
To the creatures of the sea: “fill the waters in the seas”.
After the flood, to Noah and his sons: “Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth.”
“The cloud covered the tent of meeting, וּכְבוֹד יַהְוֶה מָלֵא אֶת־הַמִּשְׁכָּן.”
Moses could not enter, because the cloud dwelt on it and the glory of Yahweh filled the tabernacle.
The cloud filled the house of Yahweh, and the priests could not stand to minister, “for the glory of Yahweh filled the house of Yahweh”.
Fire came down from heaven, and the glory of Yahweh filled the house.
“Behold, the glory of Yahweh filled the house”; also Ezk 44:4.
“His train filled (מְלֵאִים) the temple.”
“Can a man hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him? … Do I not fill (מָלֵא) the heavens and the earth?”
“They have filled the land with violence.”

senses.gloss: be full, be fulfilled (of days, years, a set time)
senses.definition: Of a time set beforehand (a pregnancy, days of purifying, a vow, a man's life, years foretold): to run its whole length, so that what waits for its end now comes.

evidence.note: “וַיִּמְלְאוּ יָמֶיהָ לָלֶדֶת, and behold, twins in her womb.”
She shall not come into the sanctuary “until the days of her purifying are full (עַד־מְלֹאת)”; also Lev 12:6.
“On the day that the days of his separation are full (מְלֹאת)”, the Nazirite comes to the door of the tent.
Forty days were fulfilled for him, “for so are fulfilled the days of embalming”.
“When your days are full (יִמְלְאוּ יָמֶיךָ) and you lie down with your fathers, I will raise up your seed after you.”
“When seventy years are full (כִמְלֹאות), I will punish the king of Babylon.”
“When seventy years for Babylon are full, I will visit you and establish my good word to you, to bring you back to this place.”
“Cry to her that her warfare is full (מָלְאָה צְבָאָהּ), that her iniquity is pardoned.”
“Our end drew near, our days are full, for our end has come.”
When those days were fulfilled, the king made a feast.
Daniel fasted “until three weeks of days were full”.
“The days were not yet full.”

senses.definition: With לֵב as subject and an infinitive: a man's heart is so full of a purpose that he does it; to dare.

evidence.note: Because sentence on an evil work is not carried out quickly, “the heart of the sons of men is full in them (מָלֵא) to do evil”.
“Who is he, and where is he, אֲשֶׁר־מְלָאוֹ לִבּוֹ לַעֲשׂוֹת כֵּן?”: whose heart has filled him to do so.
“The heart of the sons of men is full of evil, and madness is in their heart while they live.”

stems.gloss: be filled; be fulfilled; be satisfied

senses.definition: To be made full, or filled with something: the earth with violence, the land with a people, with water, with silver and idols, a house with smoke, a man with wisdom, the mouth with laughter, the earth with the glory of Yahweh.

evidence.note: “The earth was corrupt before God, וַתִּמָּלֵא הָאָרֶץ חָמָס.”
The sons of Israel multiplied, “and the land was filled with them”.
“You shall not see wind or rain, yet that valley shall be filled with water”; fulfilled in 2Ki 3:20.
“His land is filled with silver and gold … filled with horses … filled with idols.”
At the seraphim's cry “the house was filled with smoke”.
Hiram “was filled with wisdom and understanding and knowledge to do all work in bronze”.
“Then our mouth was filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing.”
“Your barns shall be filled with plenty.”
“Every jar shall be filled with wine.”
“As I live, all the earth shall be filled with the glory of Yahweh (וְיִמָּלֵא כְבוֹד־יַהְוֶה אֶת־כָּל־הָאָרֶץ).”
“The earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of Yahweh as the waters cover the sea.”
“Let the whole earth be filled with his glory. Amen and amen.”

senses.gloss: be filled, satisfied (the eye, the ear, the soul)
senses.definition: Of the eye, the ear or the soul, which are never filled: never satisfied. It stands in parallel with שָׂבַע.

evidence.note: “The eye is not satisfied (לֹא־תִשְׂבַּע) with seeing, nor the ear filled (לֹא־תִמָּלֵא) with hearing.”
“All the toil of man is for his mouth, and yet the soul is not filled.”

senses.definition: Of a stretch of days: to be completed.

evidence.note: “Seven days were fulfilled (וַיִּמָּלֵא) after Yahweh had struck the river.”

stems.gloss: fill; fill with (spirit, wisdom); fill the hand (install as priest); fulfil (a word); complete (a time); follow wholly; set (stones)

senses.definition: To make a thing full: a skin with water, sacks with grain, a trench with water, the hungry soul with good, a house with glory, a city with blood or with the slain.

evidence.note: Hagar “went and filled (וַתְּמַלֵּא) the skin with water and gave the boy a drink”.
Joseph commanded “to fill their sacks with grain”; also Gen 44:1.
The water ran round the altar, “and he filled the trench also with water”.
“He satisfies (הִשְׂבִּיעַ) the longing soul, and the hungry soul he fills (מִלֵּא) with good.”
“Open your mouth wide and I will fill it.”
“Yahweh is exalted … he has filled Zion with justice and righteousness.”
“I will shake all the nations, and the desire of all the nations shall come, and I will fill this house with glory.”
Aaron brought the grain offering “and filled his palm from it” and burned it on the altar.
“Feed your belly and fill your stomach with this scroll that I give you.”
Manasseh shed innocent blood “till he had filled Jerusalem from one end to another”; also 2Ki 24:4.
“You have filled me with indignation.”
Those who forsake Yahweh “fill mixed wine for Destiny”.
“Jehu filled his hand with the bow”: drew it to the full.
“I have bent Judah for me as a bow; I have filled it with Ephraim.”

senses.gloss: fill (a man) with the spirit, with wisdom
senses.definition: Yahweh fills a man with his spirit, or with wisdom of heart, so that he can do the work he is given; the spirit stands beside wisdom, understanding and knowledge as what fills him.

evidence.note: Of Bezalel: “וָאֲמַלֵּא אֹתוֹ the spirit of God, in wisdom and in understanding and in knowledge and in all workmanship.”
“All the wise of heart whom I have filled with the spirit of wisdom, that they make Aaron's garments.”
“He has filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding and in knowledge.”
“He has filled them with wisdom of heart to do all manner of work.”

senses.gloss: fill the hand (install as priest, consecrate)
senses.definition: מִלֵּא יָד “fill the hand” of a man: to install him as priest. At the installation of Aaron and his sons the fat, the right thigh and the bread of the ram of filling were put on their palms and waved before Yahweh, then burnt on the altar; the hands so filled were hands set apart to offer. The phrase then stands for the whole consecration, done over seven days, and for any setting of a man to be priest, true or false. With לַיהוָה and a man as subject, it is to consecrate oneself to Yahweh's service by bringing what is his.

evidence.note: “You shall anoint them וּמִלֵּאתָ אֶת־יָדָם and sanctify them, that they may minister to me as priests.”
“The priesthood shall be theirs for a perpetual statute, וּמִלֵּאתָ יַד־אַהֲרֹן וְיַד־בָּנָיו.”
The fat, the right thigh and the bread, “for it is a ram of filling (אֵיל מִלֻּאִים)”, are put “on the palms of Aaron and on the palms of his sons” and waved before Yahweh.
Moses “put all on the palms of Aaron and on the palms of his sons” and waved them, then took them from their palms and burnt them: “they were a filling (מִלֻּאִים) for a sweet savour”.
They eat the things by which covering was made “to fill their hand, to sanctify them”.
“Seven days you shall fill their hand.”

“You shall not go out from the door of the tent of meeting seven days, until the days of your filling are full (מְלֹאת יְמֵי מִלֻּאֵיכֶם), for seven days he shall fill your hand (יְמַלֵּא אֶת־יֶדְכֶם).”
Aaron's holy garments go to his sons after him, “to be anointed in them and to fill their hand in them”.
“The priest whom he anoints and whose hand he fills to be priest in his father's place.”
The great priest, on whose head the anointing oil was poured, “and who has had his hand filled to wear the garments”.
The sons of Aaron, “the anointed priests, whose hand he filled to be priests”.
Micah “filled the hand of one of his sons, and he became his priest”; also Jdg 17:12.
Jeroboam made priests of the high places from all the people: “whoever wished, he filled his hand, and he became one of the priests of the high places”.
“Whoever comes to fill his hand with a young bull and seven rams becomes a priest of no-gods.”
To the Levites who had stood with him: “fill your hand today for Yahweh”, for each man had been against his son and his brother.
David: “Who is willing to fill his hand today for Yahweh?”, of giving for the house.
Hezekiah: “Now you have filled your hand for Yahweh; come near and bring sacrifices.”
Of the altar: “seven days they shall make covering for the altar and cleanse it, and fill its hand (וּמִלְאוּ יָדָו)”.

senses.gloss: fulfil (a word, a promise, a vow, a request)
senses.definition: To bring about in full what has been spoken: Yahweh fulfils with his hand what he spoke with his mouth; men fulfil vows; Yahweh fulfils a king's petitions.

evidence.note: Solomon thrust out Abiathar from being priest “לְמַלֵּא אֶת־דְּבַר יַהְוֶה which he spoke concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh”.
“Blessed be Yahweh … who spoke with his mouth to David my father, וּבְיָדוֹ מִלֵּא.”
“You spoke with your mouth, and with your hand you have fulfilled it, as it is this day”; also 2Ch 6:4, 15.
“To fulfil the word of Yahweh by the mouth of Jeremiah, until the land had enjoyed her sabbaths … to fulfil seventy years.”
“You have spoken with your mouths and fulfilled with your hands, saying, We will surely perform our vows.”
“May he fulfil all your counsel … may Yahweh fulfil all your petitions.”
Nathan to Bathsheba: “I will come in after you and fill up (confirm) your words.”

senses.definition: To fill out a set time or number to its end.

evidence.note: Laban: “Complete (מַלֵּא) the week of this one, and we will give you the other also”; Gen 29:28, Jacob did so.
“The number of your days I will fulfil (אֲמַלֵּא).”
In the new Jerusalem there shall be no more “an old man who has not filled his days”.
Daniel understood from the books the number of years of the word of Yahweh to Jeremiah, “לְמַלֹּאות for the desolations of Jerusalem, seventy years”.
David brought the foreskins “and they gave them in full number (וַיְמַלְאוּם) to the king”.

senses.definition: מִלֵּא אַחֲרֵי יַהְוֶה: to go after Yahweh with nothing held back. It is said of Caleb and Joshua, set against the men who would not and died in the wilderness, and denied of Solomon, who turned to other gods.

evidence.note: “My servant Caleb, because there was another spirit with him and he filled after me (וַיְמַלֵּא אַחֲרָי), I will bring him into the land.”
None of the men who came up from Egypt shall see the land, “because they did not fill after me, except Caleb … and Joshua … for they filled after Yahweh”.
Caleb: “my brothers made the heart of the people melt, but I filled after Yahweh my God”; also Jos 14:9, 14.
“Solomon did evil in the eyes of Yahweh and did not fill after Yahweh, as David his father.”

senses.definition: To fill a setting with precious stones, as on the breastplate of judgment.

evidence.note: “You shall fill in it fillings of stone (וּמִלֵּאתָ בוֹ מִלֻּאַת אֶבֶן), four rows of stones.”
“They filled in it four rows of stones.”
Bezalel's skill “in cutting of stones for setting (לְמַלֹּאת)”; also Exo 35:33.

senses.definition: Beside a verb of crying out, “fill” is to do it in full voice.

evidence.note: “Blow the trumpet in the land, קִרְאוּ מַלְאוּ, and say, Assemble, and let us go into the fortified cities.”

senses.definition: Passive of setting stones: filled in, mounted.

evidence.note: “His hands are rings of gold מְמֻלָּאִים בַּתַּרְשִׁישׁ”: set with beryl.

senses.definition: Of a crowd of enemies: to gather in full number against a man.

evidence.note: “They have gaped on me with their mouth … יַחַד עָלַי יִתְמַלָּאוּן”: together against me they mass themselves.

evidence.locator: 1Ki.2.27, מַלֵּא → πληρωθῆναι; 1Ki.8.15, מִלֵּא → ἐπλήρωσεν; Jer.25.12, כִמְלֹאות → πληρωθῆναι; 2Ch.36.21 → πληρωθῆναι; Gen.25.24 → ἐπληρώθησαν; Gen.1.28 → πληρώσατε; Psa.72.19 → πληρωθήσεται; πληρόω renders מָלֵא ×48

evidence.note: “All this came to pass ἵνα πληρωθῇ what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet”: the Old Testament's “fulfil the word of Yahweh” (1Ki 2:27; 2Ch 36:21). The Peshitta has the same root, דּנֵתמַלֵא.
“I came not to destroy but πληρῶσαι”; Peshitta דֵּאמַלֵא.
“What God foretold by the mouth of all his prophets, that his Christ should suffer, he has fulfilled (ἐπλήρωσεν) so”: spoken with the mouth, fulfilled with the hand (1Ki 8:15).
“All things must be fulfilled which are written in the law of Moses and the prophets and the psalms concerning me.”
“The time is fulfilled (πεπλήρωται) and the kingdom of God has drawn near”: the time set beforehand run out, as Jer 25:12; Dan 9:2.
“Jerusalem shall be trodden down by the nations until the times of the nations are fulfilled (πληρωθῶσιν).”
The sound as of a mighty wind “filled (ἐπλήρωσεν) all the house where they were sitting”.

greek.gloss: fill; (passive) be filled, be fulfilled (of days)

evidence.locator: Exo.40.34, מָלֵא → ἐπλήσθη; Isa.6.4, יִמָּלֵא → ἐπλήσθη; Hab.2.14, תִּמָּלֵא → πλησθήσεται; 1Ki.8.11 → ἔπλησεν; πίμπλημι renders מָלֵא ×40, besides the forms the alignment leaves unlemmatised

evidence.note: “When the days of their purification according to the law of Moses were fulfilled (ἐπλήσθησαν)”: the law of Lev 12:4, 6, עַד־מְלֹאת יְמֵי טָהֳרָהּ.
“The days were fulfilled that she should give birth”: Gen 25:24, וַיִּמְלְאוּ יָמֶיהָ לָלֶדֶת.
“When the days of his service were fulfilled, he went to his house.”
“They were all filled (ἐπλήσθησαν) with holy spirit and began to speak with other tongues”: Exo 31:3, “I have filled him with the spirit of God.”
John “shall be filled with holy spirit even from his mother's womb”.

evidence.locator: Exo.28.41, וּמִלֵּאתָ אֶת־יָדָם → ἐμπλήσεις τὰς χεῖρας; Exo.31.3, וָאֲמַלֵּא → ἐνέπλησα; Num.14.21, יִמָּלֵא → ἐμπλήσει; Deu.34.9 → ἐνεπλήσθη; ἐμπίπλημι renders מָלֵא ×8, besides the forms the alignment leaves unlemmatised

evidence.note: “He has filled (ἐνέπλησεν) the hungry with good things”: Psa 107:9, וְנֶפֶשׁ רְעֵבָה מִלֵּא־טוֹב.

greek.gloss: complete, make perfect; (Septuagint) consecrate a priest

evidence.locator: Exo.29.9, וּמִלֵּאתָ יַד → τελειώσεις; Exo.29.29, לְמַלֵּא → τελειῶσαι; Exo.29.33; Exo.29.35, תְּמַלֵּא → τελειώσεις; Lev.8.33, יְמַלֵּא → τελειώσει; Lev.16.32 → τελειώσουσιν

evidence.note: “The law appoints men high priests who have weakness, but the word of the oath, which was after the law, a son, perfected (τετελειωμένον) for ever”: the Septuagint's word for filling the priest's hands, said of the son made priest.
“Having been made perfect (τελειωθείς), he became to all who obey him the cause of eternal salvation”, named by God high priest after the order of Melchizedek (Heb 5:10).
It became God “to make the leader of their salvation perfect through sufferings”.

parallels.note: “Be satisfied”: filling and satisfying the soul or the eye.
“Cover”: the cloud covered the tent and the glory filled the tabernacle; the earth filled with knowledge as the waters cover the sea.

evidence.note: “His splendour covered the heavens and his praise filled the earth.”

parallels.note: “Speak”: what is spoken with the mouth is fulfilled with the hand.
“Anoint”: anointing and filling the hand go together at the installation of a priest.

opposites.note: “Empty”: Naomi went out full and came back empty.
“Empty” vessels to be filled with the oil.
“Empty out (a sword)”: the enemy's soul shall be filled with them when he empties his sword.

phrases.gloss: fill the hand (install as priest, consecrate)
the days are full (a set time has run out)

words.summary: The adjective, “full”, about sixty times; its key's count (84) takes in some 24 tokens that are the qal of the verb, spelt alike, and the brief also files its feminine מְלֵאָה (Num 7) under the noun of that spelling.

senses.definition: Full, of a vessel, an ear of grain, a house, a field, a city; with what fills it after it.

evidence.note: “Seven ears came up on one stalk, מְלֵאֹת and good.”
Nahshon's offering: a silver dish and bowl, “both of them full (מְלֵאִים) of fine flour mixed with oil”, and a gold spoon “full of incense” (Num 7:14).
“Pour into all these vessels, and set aside the full one.”
“Houses full of all good things which you did not fill.”
“I went out full (מְלֵאָה), and Yahweh has brought me back empty (רֵיקָם).”
“All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not full.”
The valley “was full of bones”.
The rims of the wheels “full of eyes round about”; also Ezk 10:12.
“The faithful city … she was full of justice (מְלֵאֲתִי מִשְׁפָּט).”
“Woe to the bloody city, all of it full of lies and robbery.”
“Better a dry morsel with quietness than a house full of sacrifices with strife.”
“How the bones grow in the womb of her who is full (הַמְּלֵאָה)”: the pregnant woman.

senses.definition: Of a man: full of the spirit of wisdom, of wisdom, of the blessing of Yahweh.

evidence.note: “Joshua the son of Nun was full of the spirit of wisdom (מָלֵא רוּחַ חָכְמָה), for Moses had laid his hands on him.”
“Naphtali, satisfied (שְׂבַע) with favour and full of the blessing of Yahweh.”
The king of Tyre, “full of wisdom and perfect in beauty”.

senses.definition: Of silver paid: the full price, nothing taken off.

evidence.note: Abraham: “for the full silver (בְּכֶסֶף מָלֵא) let him give it to me for a burying place.”
David to Ornan: “give it to me for the full silver … I will surely buy it for the full silver, for I will not offer burnt offerings without cost.”

senses.definition: Used as an adverb: fully, all of it, with full voice.

evidence.note: “Your brothers … they have called after you מָלֵא”: aloud, in full cry.
“They shall be devoured as dry stubble מָלֵא”: wholly.
“A wind fuller (מָלֵא) than these shall come for me.”

evidence.locator: Isa.6.3, מְלֹא → πλήρης; Ezk.44.4, מָלֵא → πλήρης; πλήρης renders מָלֵא ×59 and מְלֹא ×7

evidence.note: “Jesus, full (πλήρης) of holy spirit, returned from the Jordan”: as Joshua was “full of the spirit of wisdom” (Deu 34:9). The Peshitta has מלֵא.
“Seven men of good report, full of holy spirit and wisdom”; Peshitta וַמלֵין.
Stephen, “full of holy spirit”, saw the glory of God.
“We beheld his glory … full of grace and truth”; Peshitta דַּמלֵא.

words.gloss: fullness, what fills; a full measure; a multitude

senses.gloss: fullness, all that fills (the earth, the sea, a city)
senses.definition: Everything that fills a place: the earth and all in it, the sea and all in it, a land and its people.

evidence.note: “To Yahweh is the earth וּמְלוֹאָהּ, the world and those who dwell in it.”
“If I were hungry I would not tell you, for the world is mine וּמְלֹאָהּ.”
“The world and its fullness, you founded them.”
Joseph's blessing: “the precious things of the earth and its fullness”.
“They have come and devoured the land and its fullness, the city and those who dwell in it.”
“They shall overflow the land and its fullness, the city and those who dwell in it.”
“Hear, all you peoples; give ear, O earth, and its fullness.”
“Let the sea roar, and its fullness”; also Psa 98:7; 1Ch 16:32; Isa 42:10.
“Holy, holy, holy is Yahweh of hosts; מְלֹא כָל־הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ”: the fullness of all the earth is his glory.
The spread of its wings shall fill “the breadth of your land, O Immanuel”.

senses.gloss: a full measure (a handful, an omer full, the full length)
senses.definition: As much as fills a vessel, a hand or a house; the whole length of a cord, a reed, a man.

evidence.note: “Put there מְלֹא הָעֹמֶר of manna, and lay it up before Yahweh.”
The priest “shall take from it his handful (מְלֹא קֻמְצוֹ) of its fine flour”.
“A censer full of coals of fire … and his hands full of sweet incense.”
“Take handfuls (מְלֹא חָפְנֵיכֶם) of ashes of the furnace.”
The widow: “only a handful of flour in the jar.”
“Better is a handful with quietness than two hands full with toil.”
Balaam: “if Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold”; also Num 24:13.
Gideon wrung from the fleece “a bowl full of water”.
David measured Moab with the line, “and one full line to keep alive”.
The foundations of the side chambers were “a full reed (מְלוֹ הַקָּנֶה) of six cubits”.
Saul fell at once “his full length (מְלֹא־קוֹמָתוֹ) on the earth”.

senses.definition: Of people: a whole company, a multitude.

evidence.note: Of Ephraim: “his seed shall become מְלֹא־הַגּוֹיִם”, a multitude of nations.
“As a lion growls over its prey, when מְלֹא רֹעִים is called out against it”: a whole band of shepherds.

evidence.locator: Psa.24.1, וּמְלוֹאָהּ → τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς; Psa.50.12; Psa.89.12; Psa.96.11; πλήρωμα renders מְלֹא ×5

evidence.note: Psa 24:1 quoted: “the earth is the Lord's and its fullness (τὸ πλήρωμα αὐτῆς)”; the Peshitta has בַּמלָאָה.
“When the fullness of the time (τὸ πλήρωμα τοῦ χρόνου) came, God sent forth his son, born of a woman”: the set time full, as Gen 25:24.
“Until the fullness of the nations comes in”; Peshitta מֻולָיָא.
“In him it pleased all the fullness to dwell”; Peshitta מֻולָיָא.

words.summary: Three times, of the full produce of field and vat, from which Israel brought its first portion to Yahweh. The brief counts 24 tokens under this key, but 21 of them (Num 7, 2Sa 23:11, 2Ki 7:15 and others) are the feminine of the adjective מָלֵא, “full”.

senses.gloss: full yield, the fullness of the harvest
senses.definition: The full produce of the threshing floor, the winepress or the sown field.

evidence.note: “You shall not delay מְלֵאָתְךָ and your juice; the firstborn of your sons you shall give to me.”
The Levites' offering “shall be reckoned to you as the grain of the threshing floor וְכַמְלֵאָה מִן־הַיָּקֶב”: as the fullness of the winepress.
“You shall not sow your vineyard with two kinds, lest הַמְלֵאָה of the seed which you have sown and the yield of the vineyard become holy.”

words.summary: Always plural. Of the priests, the noun of “fill the hand”: the ram, the bread and the days of their installation. Of stones, the fillings of the ephod and breastplate: their settings.

senses.gloss: filling (of the hands), installation of priests
senses.definition: The installation of Aaron and his sons as priests: the ram whose portions filled their hands (אֵיל הַמִּלֻּאִים), the offering itself, and the seven days it lasted.

evidence.note: “The right thigh, for it is a ram of filling (אֵיל מִלֻּאִים).”
Taken from their palms and burnt: “they were a filling (מִלֻּאִים) for a sweet savour”.
“Until the days of your filling (מִלֻּאֵיכֶם) are full, for seven days he shall fill your hand.”
The breast and the thigh of the ram of filling, which is for Aaron and his sons.
“You shall take the ram of filling and boil its flesh in a holy place”; also Exo 29:34.
“This is the law of the burnt offering … and of the filling (וְלַמִּלּוּאִים).”
“The second ram, the ram of filling”, on whose head Aaron and his sons laid their hands.
“The bread that is in the basket of the filling.”

senses.definition: Stones that fill a setting, for the ephod and the breastplate.

evidence.note: “Onyx stones, and stones of filling (אַבְנֵי מִלֻּאִים), for the ephod and for the breastplate”; also Exo 35:9, 27.
David prepared for the house “onyx stones and stones to be set (וּמִלּוּאִים)”.

greek.gloss: completion, perfection; (Septuagint) consecration of a priest

evidence.locator: Exo.29.22, אֵיל מִלֻּאִים → τελείωσις; Exo.29.26, 27, 31, 34; Lev.7.37; Lev.8.22, 28, 29, 31, 33 → τελειώσεως

evidence.note: “If τελείωσις were through the Levitical priesthood … what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melchizedek?”: the Septuagint's word for the מִלֻּאִים of Aaron's installation.

senses.definition: The gold setting that a stone of the breastplate fills.

evidence.note: “You shall fill in it מִלֻּאַת אֶבֶן, four rows of stones.”
“They shall be set in gold in their fillings (בְּמִלּוּאֹתָם).”

words.summary: Once, in the Song, and its sense is not fixed by the verse: the eyes are doves “sitting on מִלֵּאת”, either the full water of the streams beside them or, as the stones of the beloved's hands in Sng 5:14, a setting that the eye fills. Either reading is a sense of filling, but since the verse does not settle which, no cognate or sibling sense is named for it, and the root's cognates count against it: the negative balance says only that its own sense is unclear, not that it belongs to another root.

senses.definition: That on which the doves sit: the brimming water of the streams, or the setting in which the eyes sit like stones.

evidence.note: “His eyes are like doves by the streams of water, washed with milk, יֹשְׁבוֹת עַל־מִלֵּאת.”
Two verses on, “his hands are rings of gold set (מְמֻלָּאִים) with beryl”.

senses.definition: To fill a place: the stone that struck the image grew and filled the whole earth.

evidence.note: “The stone that struck the image became a great mountain וּמְלָת כָּל־אַרְעָא.”

senses.definition: To be filled with a passion.

evidence.note: “Then Nebuchadnezzar הִתְמְלִי חֱמָא, and the form of his face was changed.”

words.gloss: be full, fill; fulfil; be filled; be fulfilled; complete
words.summary: The Peshitta's ܡܠܐ, used where the Greek has πληρόω and πίμπλημι: in the peal “be full”, the pael “fill, fulfil”, the ethpeel “be filled”, the ethpaal “be fulfilled” (of words and of days), and the shaphel and eshtaphal “complete, be completed”. The New Testament's formula “that it might be fulfilled” is in the Peshitta the same root as Hebrew לְמַלֵּא אֶת־דְּבַר יַהְוֶה.

stems.gloss: be full, full of; be fulfilled (of years)

senses.gloss: be full, full of (the spirit, grace)
senses.definition: To be full: a net, a man of holy spirit and wisdom, of grace and truth; of years, to run out.

evidence.note: “When it was full (מלָת), they drew it to the shore.”
“Jesus, being full (מלֵא) of holy spirit, returned from the Jordan.”
“Seven men … full (וַמלֵין) of the spirit of the Lord and wisdom.”
Stephen “full of faith and holy spirit” saw the glory of God.
“Full (דַּמלֵא) of grace and truth.”
“When forty years were fulfilled (מלַי) for him there”, the angel appeared in the bush.

senses.gloss: fulfil (the law, what the prophets foretold); fill up
senses.definition: To fulfil what is spoken or commanded; to fill up a measure.

evidence.note: “I came not to loose (the law) but to fulfil (דֵּאמַלֵא).”
“What God foretold by the mouth of all the prophets, that his Messiah should suffer, he has fulfilled (מַלִי) so.”
“From Jerusalem round about to Illyricum I have fulfilled (וֵאמַלֵא) the gospel of the Messiah.”
“Fill up (מַלַו) the measure of your fathers.”

senses.gloss: be filled (with holy spirit, joy, a sound, smoke)
senses.definition: To be filled: a house with a sound or a fragrance, men with holy spirit and joy, the temple with smoke from the glory of God.

evidence.note: “They were all filled (וֵאתמלִיו) with holy spirit and began to speak in tongues.”
“The whole house where they were sitting was filled (וֵאתמלִי) with it.”
John “shall be filled (נֵתמלֵא) with holy spirit from his mother's womb”.
“They were all filled with holy spirit and spoke the word of God with boldness.”
“The disciples were filled (מֵתמלֵין) with joy and holy spirit”: joy and spirit filling alike.
“Be not drunk with wine … but be filled (אֵתמלַו) with the spirit.”
“The house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment.”
“The temple was filled (וֵאתמלִי) with smoke from the glory of God and from his power, and no one could enter the temple”: as Exo 40:35; 1Ki 8:11; Isa 6:4.

senses.gloss: be fulfilled (what was spoken; the days)
senses.definition: Of a word of the prophets: to come to pass in full. Of a set number of days: to be completed.

evidence.note: “All this came to pass דּנֵתמַלֵא what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet.”
“That it might be fulfilled (דּנֵתמַלֵא) … Out of Egypt I called my son.”
“How then would the scriptures be fulfilled (נֵתמַלֻון), that it must be so?”
“That the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled (דּתֵתמַלֵא).”
“When the days of their purification were fulfilled (אֵתמַלִיו) according to the law of Moses”: Lev 12:4, 6.
“Her days were fulfilled (אֵתמַלִיו) that she should give birth.”
“That you may be filled (ותֵתמַלֻון) with all the fullness of God.”

senses.gloss: complete, fulfil (a ministry); fill (all in all)
senses.definition: To carry a work through to its end; of God, to fill all things.

evidence.note: To Archippus: “take heed to the ministry which you received in our Lord, that you fulfil it (משַמלֵא).”
The ecclesia, “his body, and the fullness of him who fills (משַמלֵא) all in all”.
“That my joy may be complete (משַמליָא) in them.”

senses.definition: To be brought to its full end.

evidence.note: “That my joy may be in you and your joy may be complete (ותֵשתַּמלֵא).”
Seven last plagues, “for in them the wrath of God is completed (אֵשתַּמליַת)”.
No one could enter the temple “until the seven plagues … were completed (דּנֵשתַּמליָן)”.

senses.definition: That which fills a thing up completely: the full number of the nations, the fullness that dwells in the Messiah and with which God fills believers; and of the law, its fulfilment.

evidence.note: “Love does no evil to its neighbour, because love is the fulfilment (מֻולָיֵה) of the law.”
“Blindness of heart has come upon Israel in part, until the fullness (מֻולָיָא) of the nations comes in.”
“In him it pleased all the fullness to dwell.”
“In him dwells all the fullness of the godhead bodily.”
“That you may be filled with all the fullness (מֻולָיָא) of God.”

senses.definition: All that fills the earth, in Paul's quotation of Psa 24:1.

evidence.note: “For the earth is the Lord's בַּמלָאָה”: and its fullness, Psa 24:1, וּמְלוֹאָהּ.

words.gloss: fullness; a patch (what fills up a hole)

senses.definition: Fullness, of the Word; and a patch, the piece that fills up a torn garment.

evidence.note: “From his fullness (מַליֻותֵה) we have all received, and grace for grace.”
No one puts new cloth on an old garment, “lest its filling (מַליֻותָה) tear away from that garment, and the rent be greater”.

words.summary: A noun of the shaphel, “completion, fullness”.

senses.definition: The full measure of a thing brought to completion.

evidence.note: The ecclesia, “his body, and the fullness (ושֻומלָיָא) of him who fills all in all”.
“Until we all become … one perfect man, in the measure of the stature of the fullness (דּשֻומלָיֵה) of the Messiah.”

cognates.gloss: be(come) full; (D) fill, fill up, complete, fulfil; pay; hand over, entrust
cognates.note: One of the commonest Akkadian verbs, in every period. Its range runs as the Hebrew's does, from being full and filling to completing and fulfilling; the D stem (umalli, as the Hebrew piel) is the transitive “fill”. Its senses “hand over, entrust” are worth setting beside “fill the hand”, though the glossary does not show the idiom.

evidence.locator: armep x000010160, malû [be(come) full] V
evidence.note: Meanings in the glossaries: be(come) full, be(come) filled with, fill, fill up, complete, fulfil, pay, reimburse, hand over, entrust, deliver; norms umalli, umallû, imlû, malû; 2,123 instances.

cognates.note: The adjective, as מָלֵא is both verb and adjective.

evidence.note: Meanings: full, filled, filling, completed, covered; 651 instances.

evidence.locator: armep x000102300, malû [abundance] N
evidence.note: Meanings: abundance, fullness; 33 instances.

cognates.note: A noun of malû for what fills a space in a crafted object: inlay and mountings. It answers to מִלֻּאִים and מִלֻּאָה, the stones that fill the settings of the ephod and breastplate, and to the piel and pual “set (stones)”.

evidence.locator: armep x000031350, tamlītu [filling] N
evidence.note: Meanings: decoration, filling, inlay; 51 instances. A second glossary entry (armep x000143640) gives decoration, mounting, mountings.

cognates.note: Phoenician and Punic use the piel, as Hebrew does, for filling (the granaries of Paʿr, in the Karatepe inscription) and for paying in full.

cognates.gloss: fill; complete; (causative) fill in; grant, fulfil a request
cognates.note: Sabaean: the god “would fill their canals in two rainstorms”; “they built and completed their tomb”; and in the causative, of a god, to grant or fulfil what was asked of him, as Yahweh fulfils petitions in Psa 20:6.

cognates.note: Sabaean nouns of the root: “the period (fullness) of seven years”, “a pasture whose capacity is 170 sheep”, and the yield of land; the last answers to מְלֵאָה, the full produce of the field.

It is set beside the hithpael of Job 16:10, “together they mass themselves against me”, and מְלֹא “a whole company” (Isa 31:4), but whether the sense came from “fill” is not shown, so it is recorded as possible.

cognates.note: The Targums use it where the Hebrew has מָלֵא: Onkelos at Gen 1:22, “fill the waters”, and at Exo 40:34, the glory filled the tabernacle.

evidence.note: “to fill. Targ. Gen. I, 22 … Ithpe. to be filled, full. Targ. Gen. VI, 13. Targ. Ex. XL, 34.”

cognates.note: The Targum's noun, at Onkelos Deu 33:16 for “the earth and its fullness”.

evidence.note: “Targ. Y. Num. XXXV, 17. Targ. O. Deut. XXXIII, 16.”

doctrine.statement: God blessed the first man and woman, “fill the earth and subdue it” (Gen 1:28). The earth was filled instead with violence (Gen 6:11, 13), and God destroyed all flesh with the earth in the flood, then said again to Noah and his sons, “fill the earth” (Gen 9:1). When Israel refused to go into the land, Yahweh swore, “as I live, all the earth shall be filled with the glory of Yahweh”, and that none of the men who had seen his glory and tested him should see the land (Num 14:21–23). The prophets say when: under the shoot from the stump of Jesse, who will judge the poor with righteousness and slay the wicked with the breath of his lips, “they shall not hurt or destroy in all my holy mountain, for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of Yahweh as the waters cover the sea” (Isa 11:1–9); “the earth shall be filled with the knowledge of the glory of Yahweh” (Hab 2:14); the psalm of the king who rules from sea to sea ends, “let the whole earth be filled with his glory” (Psa 72:8, 19). In Nebuchadnezzar's dream the stone that struck the image “became a great mountain and filled all the earth”, and Daniel explains: “the God of heaven will set up a kingdom which shall never be destroyed … it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever” (Dan 2:35, 44). Jesus taught his disciples to pray, “your kingdom come, your will be done, as in heaven, so on earth” (Mat 6:10), and in Revelation the voices in heaven say, “the kingdom of the world has become our Lord's and his Christ's, and he shall reign for ever” (Rev 11:15). From the verses: the earth that God made to be filled with men, and that men filled with violence, will be filled with his glory and with the knowledge of him, not by a gradual spread but when the kingdom God sets up, in the hand of the son of David, breaks the kingdoms of men and fills the whole earth.

When the tabernacle was finished, “the cloud covered the tent of meeting and the glory of Yahweh filled the tabernacle”, so that Moses could not enter (Exo 40:34–35); at the dedication of Solomon's house the priests could not stand to minister, “for the glory of Yahweh filled the house” (1Ki 8:10–11; 2Ch 7:1–2). Isaiah saw the house filled with smoke while the seraphim cried that the fullness of all the earth is his glory (Isa 6:3–4). Ezekiel saw that glory leave the house, and then saw it come back by the east gate: “behold, the glory of Yahweh filled the house” (Ezk 43:5; 44:4). By Haggai, Yahweh promised the house built after the exile, “I will shake all nations, and the desire of all nations shall come, and I will fill this house with glory” (Hag 2:7). In Revelation, before the last plagues, “the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from his power, and no one could enter the temple” (Rev 15:8). From the verses: Yahweh's filling his house with glory marks his acceptance of the dwelling made for him, and the prophets look to a house yet to be filled with glory when the nations come to it.

Scripture speaks of Yahweh's word as something spoken and then fulfilled. Solomon thrust out Abiathar “to fulfil the word of Yahweh which he spoke concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh” (1Ki 2:27), a word given generations before (1Sa 2:31–35). At the dedication he blessed Yahweh, “who spoke with his mouth to David my father, and with his hand has fulfilled it” (1Ki 8:15, 24). Jeremiah gave the exile a length, “when seventy years are full” (Jer 25:12; 29:10); Daniel read the number in the books and prayed (Dan 9:2–3); and the Chronicler says the land kept its sabbaths “to fulfil the word of Yahweh by the mouth of Jeremiah … to fulfil seventy years” (2Ch 36:21). The New Testament uses the same language of Jesus: “all this came to pass that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet” (Mat 1:22), and the Peshitta writes it with the same root, דּנֵתמַלֵא. Jesus said he came “not to destroy, but to fulfil” the law and the prophets (Mat 5:17), and after his resurrection, that “all things must be fulfilled which are written in the law of Moses and in the prophets and in the psalms concerning me” (Luk 24:44); Peter, that what God “foretold by the mouth of all his prophets, that his Christ should suffer, he has thus fulfilled” (Act 3:18). From the verses: what God speaks he brings about in full and at the time he sets; the sufferings of Christ were not a failure of the plan but the fulfilment of it, and the promises not yet fulfilled will be, as surely as the seventy years were.

Aaron and his sons were made priests by washing, clothing and anointing, and by filling their hands (Exo 28:41; 29:9). The rite shows what the words mean: the fat, the right thigh and the bread of “the ram of filling” were put on their palms and waved before Yahweh, then burnt on the altar (Exo 29:22–25; Lev 8:27–28), and this went on seven days, “until the days of your filling are full” (Lev 8:33). Others filled their own hands, or other men's, without Yahweh's call: Micah his son (Jdg 17:5), Jeroboam “whoever wished” (1Ki 13:33), so that any who came with a bull and seven rams “became a priest of no-gods” (2Ch 13:9). Hebrews says the same: “no one takes this honour to himself, but he who is called by God, as Aaron was; so also the Christ did not glorify himself to become high priest” (Heb 5:4–5). Where the Septuagint renders “fill the hand” and “filling” it uses τελειόω and τελείωσις, the words Hebrews takes up: “if perfection (τελείωσις) were through the Levitical priesthood, what further need that another priest should arise after the order of Melchizedek?” (Heb 7:11); “the law appoints men high priests who have weakness, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, a son, perfected (τετελειωμένον) for ever” (Heb 7:28); “being made perfect, he became the cause of eternal salvation to all who obey him, named by God high priest” (Heb 5:9–10). From the verses: a priest's hands were filled with the offering he was to bring, by God's appointment, over the set days; Jesus, called by God and not by himself, was made perfect as priest through what he suffered, and his priesthood, unlike Aaron's, does not pass to another.

Yahweh “filled” Bezalel “with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge and in all workmanship” (Exo 31:3; 35:31); of the other craftsmen he says, “I have filled them with the spirit of wisdom” (Exo 28:3) and “with wisdom of heart” (Exo 35:35), and of Hiram, with no mention of spirit, that “he was filled with wisdom and understanding and knowledge” (1Ki 7:14). Joshua “was full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands on him” (Deu 34:9); Micah was “full of power, the spirit of Yahweh, and justice and might” (Mic 3:8). The New Testament speaks the same way: men were “filled with holy spirit” (Act 2:4; 4:31), “full of holy spirit and wisdom” (Act 6:3), “filled with joy and holy spirit” (Act 13:52), and are told, “be not drunk with wine, but be filled with the spirit” (Eph 5:18). From the verses: the spirit is spoken of as what fills a man, alongside wisdom, knowledge, power, joy and indignation (Jer 15:17); it is God's power given to men for the work he sets them, not a person who fills them.

“The earth is Yahweh's and its fullness (מְלוֹאָהּ)” (Psa 24:1), and Paul quotes it (1Co 10:26). Of Jesus he writes that “it pleased (the Father) that in him all the fullness should dwell” (Col 1:19), and “in him dwells all the fullness of the godhead bodily” (Col 2:9); John, that the Word made flesh was “full of grace and truth” and “of his fullness we have all received” (Jhn 1:14, 16). The same fullness is prayed for believers: “that you may be filled with all the fullness of God” (Eph 3:19), and the ecclesia is “his body, the fullness of him who fills all in all” (Eph 1:23), growing “to the measure of the stature of the fullness of the Christ” (Eph 4:13). The Peshitta uses words of this root throughout (מֻולָיָא, מַליֻותָא, שֻומלָיָא). From the verses: the fullness that dwelt in Jesus was God's, placed in him because it pleased the Father; it is the same fullness believers are to be filled with, which shows it is not a second person of the godhead but the Father's character and power dwelling in his son, a man.

Of the twelve spies only Caleb and Joshua “filled after Yahweh” (Num 14:24; 32:12), while the men who did not were sworn not to see the land (Num 32:11); Caleb said of himself, “my brothers made the heart of the people melt, but I filled after Yahweh my God”, and Hebron became his inheritance “because he filled after Yahweh” (Jos 14:8, 14). Of Solomon it is written that he “did not fill after Yahweh, as David his father”, when his wives turned his heart after other gods (1Ki 11:4, 6). From the verses: Yahweh asks to be followed with nothing held back, and the inheritance is promised to those who so follow him; a divided heart, even in the wisest king, is what scripture calls not following him fully.

Imlah (יִמְלָה/יִמְלָא, m.bz.ai, j.bq.af) is drafted as names/imlah.json. m.bz.ao (מְלוֹ) is a zero-token cross-reference to מְלֹא (Ezk 41:8 is counted under m.bz.ac). The brief's stem labels follow the corpus: the qal-tagged מָלֵא forms with an object (Exo 40:34; 1Ki 8:10) are verbs, the untagged ones (Num 7) adjectives. Peshitta stems are read from the vocalised forms (pael דֵּאמַלֵא, ethpeel וֵאתמלִי, ethpaal דּנֵתמַלֵא, shaphel משַמלֵא, eshtaphal ותֵשתַּמלֵא) and SEDRA's form codes for lexeme 1765 (MLA); the Peshitta uses שׁלם, not מלא, at Mrk 1:15, Luk 4:21, Gal 4:4, Jhn 19:24 and Jas 2:23. Ugaritic (Segert) and Sabaean (Biella) readings are from OCR only and the PDFs were not rendered; check the forms before review. Leads not followed: Ge'ez mälʾa “fill, be full” (Dillmann, Leslau; no local copy, no locator verified); CAD M/1 malû, especially whether Akkadian has a “fill the hand” idiom for entrusting or installing (Oracc lists “hand over, entrust” among malû's meanings but not the idiom); DULAT for Ugaritic mlʾ, mlu, mlat; Payne Smith for the Syriac nouns; the Mari and Old Babylonian “fill the hand” comparisons sometimes cited for מִלֵּא יָד. Open questions: (1) מִלֵּאת (Sng 5:12) is left with two readings; (2) the Arabic “conspire together” and “assembly” are recorded only as possible for the hithpael of Job 16:10 and מְלֹא “multitude”; (3) the doctrine items kingdom-of-god, filling-the-hand, spirit-is-gods-power and fullness-in-christ are reasoned conclusions for review.
